extracted.intended_audience: writers querying literary agents (especially book authors — YA/MG/adult fiction and nonfiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors preparing query letters and non-fiction book proposals to send to literary agents, with examples and resources for platform building and manuscript critique. Emphasizes reading individual agency guidelines and learning from sample successful queries/proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read agency guidelines before querying
rubrics_metrics.description: to read agency guidelines before you send your query to anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction to check each agent's submission guidelines since requirements vary; this is presented as a primary, non-negotiable step before sending queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize subjectivity of querying
rubrics_metrics.description: Just remember... it's all subjective, and ... Everyone wants something different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set expectation that there is no single correct approach — different agents prefer different elements (so tailor queries rather than expecting one universal template).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative titles only when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of us like comparative titles, some agents don't care about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative titles (i.e., likening your book to existing titles) are optional and agent-dependent; check guidelines or agent preferences before including them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include brief author bio only if requested/preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agents want a brief bio, others don't.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author bio is optional depending on agent; if the agent's guidelines request or indicate preference for a bio, include a concise one, otherwise omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from annotated example query letters
rubrics_metrics.description: I'm lucky enough to have worked with authors who were willing to let me share their query letters here on my website. It's my hope that their query letters will help you out ... by letting you see an example of a query done right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the linked sample queries (each labeled with genre) and the agent's notes about why those pitches worked. Use them as models for tone, length, hook, and structure rather than copying. Examples include queries for YA contemporary, YA sci-fi/fantasy, adult literary sci‑fi, memoir, non-fiction, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study detailed non-fiction proposal examples
rubrics_metrics.description: In this guide, I showcase pieces of the actual non-fiction book proposal. It’s detailed, and I hope it helps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonfiction projects, examine the provided proposal breakdowns (cookbook, pop-culture history, kid-lit nonfiction, essay collections, wellness/self-help, memoir-in-essays, etc.) to learn expected proposal elements and level of detail. The page highlights concrete sample proposals (e.g., Are You Afraid of the Dark Rum; 8-Bit Apocalypse; Eat to Feed) to model structure and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a roundup of freelance editors/critique providers for manuscript notes
rubrics_metrics.description: I keep a roundup of authors and editors in the industry who work on dishing out freelance critiques and manuscript notes! It’s been updated as of January 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before querying, consider getting professional manuscript notes or freelance critiques. The agent provides an updated list of vetted freelancers/editors to help improve your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build platform and use social media strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: I also have a few blog posts full of advice about other things too, particularly platform and social media, that you might find helpful: A Beginner’s Guide to Looking Up Literary Agents; A Beginner’s Guide to Writing IP; Ten Tips on Using Social Media From a Literary Agent; Reasons to Use Social Media That Have Nothing to Do With Selling Books; Building Your Platform For Yourself, Not Your Book; Ways to Build Your Platform That Have Nothing to Do with Your Twitter Following.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the linked posts to learn how to cultivate an author platform and use social media in ways that support a writing career (not solely for immediate book sales). Advice covers researching agents, intellectual property basics, social media best practices, and platform-building strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor examples and agent posts for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Check back often! As titles get closer to publication, I check in with my authors about publishing their query letters!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly revisit the agent's resources because new, annotated query letters and proposal examples may be posted as authors' titles approach publication; staying current helps you see contemporary, successful pitches.
